leads.summary: A skip can expire while the lid is closed and cause logind to suspend without another close
leads.consequence: If the user arms skip-once, closes the lid and leaves a task running without a working herdr agent, the daemon removes the flag after 30 minutes and releases its handle-lid-switch inhibitor even though the lid remains closed. systemd logind continuously rechecks closed lids, not only closure edges, so it can suspend as soon as the inhibitor drops. This contradicts 'skip next lid close only, consumed on reopen' and can terminate work later in the same closed-lid session. Apply TTL only until the first close, then keep the lock until reopen (or make mid-close expiry an explicit documented policy).
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Opus lower-severity note: TTL counts from arming, closed lid suspends on expiry. Not published (documented design: disarms after 30 min).

leads.summary: The packaged settings recipe omits the new user service
leads.consequence: Installing the PR's runtime scripts does not install /usr/lib/systemd/user/omarchy-lid-guard.service. The first-run batch enable fails under set -e (not just this feature), and the existing-install migration prints an error yet returns success and is marked done, so installing a fixed package later will not retry it. The toggle can still record the flag and notify that the next close is safe, while no guard is watching.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Opus F4; published in More findings with static check.

leads.summary: The wakeup signal also kills the inhibitor
leads.consequence: systemctl kill defaults to all service processes, not the main daemon alone. Whenever skip-once or allow pokes the active unit it delivers USR1 to its background systemd-inhibit/sleep process as well; these processes do not have the guard's USR1 trap. The currently held low-level lock drops, with a race before reconciliation replaces it. Logind rechecks a closed lid continuously, so a poke made while the lid is already closed can also trigger a suspend without a second closure. Specify --kill-whom=main and test inhibitor continuity around the signal.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Opus F5 reproduced; published as optional note.

leads.summary: The separate guard locks a docked clamshell after the existing handler deliberately declines
leads.consequence: When an external display is connected and an agent is working on AC (or a skip was armed), the Hyprland lid close invokes omarchy-system-lid-close, which skips the lock for a docked clamshell, but on the next 5s guard poll the new open-to-closed branch locks anyway. This interrupts ongoing work on the external screen, contrary to the existing docked policy. Use the same external-monitor predicate as the existing handler.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Opus F3 reproduced; published in More findings.

leads.summary: Open PR #12210 replaces logind lid handling and adds the same test filename
leads.consequence: #12210 makes logind ignore lid events and has omarchy-system-lid-close start omarchy-system-lid-suspend, which calls systemctl suspend after its delay without inspecting low-level handle-lid-switch inhibitors. If it and this PR both merge, the guard still reports a held inhibitor while that separate suspend bypasses it. Both also add distinct files at test/shell.d/lid-suspend-test.sh, so one test body will be lost or require combining. Adjust the other suspend helper to respect guard state (or share a single gating mechanism) and combine both test suites.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; #12210 overlap in Opus report; published in optional note.

It therefore passes without detecting PACKAGE. Add (source, /usr/lib/systemd/user/omarchy-lid-guard.service, systemd/user/omarchy-lid-guard.service) to package_defaults in config-test.sh:152-153.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; config-test.sh package_defaults; merged into F4 text (duplicate of PACKAGE).

leads.summary: The toggle promises restored lid suspend even while the automatic agent guard is holding it
leads.consequence: With an agent working on AC and no manual flag, `omarchy toggle lid-suspend status` says 'no skip armed: lid close suspends normally' immediately before printing the active guard and its inhibitor. Likewise `allow` says 'Next lid close suspends again' after clearing the flag although the daemon simply changes its reason to agents working on AC and keeps blocking. Distinguish manual flag status from actual lid policy and make notifications conditional or qualified.
leads.triage: verified_by_coordinator; Diff lines (toggle cmd_allow/cmd_status) print 'suspends again/normally' regardless of agent guard. Confirmed; low value, not published (3-note cap).

leads.summary: Laptops without /proc/acpi/button/lid cannot start the guard, even if logind has a lid switch
leads.consequence: On Apple Silicon SMC lid devices without an ACPI lid path, the unit's ConditionPathExists fails; a skipped unit is not an active guard. The toggle does not check for this condition and still reports that the next lid close will not suspend. Existing open #7951 adds logind-based lid-state detection for this hardware and #13661 adds Hyprland SMC lid binds, neither makes the guard's ACPI condition true. Confirm on an Apple Silicon machine or with upstream Linux/Asahi source for the exact procfs and evdev exposure before calling it universal.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Opus gating-mismatch note (#7951); hypothesis, not published.

# RETRO: PR #11525 (team 4)

## What worked

- The brief explicitly banned running herdr, systemctl and the lock on the host. This mattered because the review infrastructure itself runs on herdr. The reviewers stubbed all of them.
- The Opus self-check caught two wrong details: the missing `|| true` and the conflict cause. It also caught three overstatements before editorial.

## Friction

- The Sol hunt took 87 minutes against the expected 15 to 25. Its turn count stalled for about 20 minutes twice while output kept streaming.
- `visible_length` uses a non-greedy `<details>` regex, so nested `<details>` blocks are counted wrongly (2299 visible instead of about 1600). The workaround was to un-nest the blocks. **Tool bug:** handle nesting, or reject nested blocks explicitly.
- Editorial check 1 returned "pass" with a non-blocking issue. `check-result` raised "Contradictory pass with issues" and the check had to be rerun. **Tool/prompt gap:** allow advisory notes on a pass, or instruct the checker to use revise.
- The editorial checker flagged sandbox PIDs in verbatim reproducer output as private data. This conflicts with the "never edit output" rule. The workaround was a provenance label in the summary. **Feature request:** state in comment-requirements that review.py sandbox PIDs and timestamps are synthetic.
- The coordinator's assembly edit used an unquoted heredoc, which expanded backticks. Use quoted heredocs or the Edit tool.

## Carry forward

- Assemble drafts from a template with verbatim reproducer includes (`coord/assemble.py`).

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** When the working agents change, the guard kills its inhibitor before starting a new one, so an undocked closed lid can suspend.

### Reason change drops the inhibitor

The `--why` text names the working agents, and a changed reason runs `stop_inhibitor` before `start_inhibitor` (also when a skip expires while an agent works). **Impact:** logind rechecks a closed lid on every event (systemd source, not run), so an undocked lid on AC can suspend in the gap.

**Suggested change:** Keep a live inhibitor while any reason applies; use a fixed `--why`.

# Reproducer: a change in which agents are working kills the held inhibitor before starting the next one

Reviewed head: 20a9407982acf04ae068b3faf545782abf49ba56 (also fails identically with the PR merged into quattro 8b4eae66).

`reconcile` puts the working agents' names in the inhibitor's reason (`agents working on AC: $names`). When the reason text changes while an inhibitor is alive, it runs `stop_inhibitor` and then `start_inhibitor`. So the lid is briefly not inhibited. That happens when one of several agents finishes or a second agent starts, and also when an armed skip expires while an agent works.

Save as `test/shell.d/lid-guard-reason-change-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/lid-guard-reason-change-test.sh`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

guard="$ROOT/bin/omarchy-system-lid-guard"
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
pidfile=""

cleanup() {
  [[ -n $pidfile && -f $pidfile ]] && kill "$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$pidfile")" 2>/dev/null || true
  [[ -n ${first_pid:-} ]] && kill "$first_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -rf "$tmpdir"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

export HOME="$tmpdir/home" XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$tmpdir/runtime" AGENTS="$tmpdir/agents"
export OMARCHY_LID_STATE_GLOB="$tmpdir/lid/state"
pidfile="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-lid-guard/inhibit.pid"
mkdir -p "$HOME" "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR" "$tmpdir/bin" "$tmpdir/lid"

# Lid closed, undocked, on AC. While the lid stays closed logind re-checks it
# on every event, so any moment without a handle-lid-switch inhibitor suspends.
echo "state:      closed" >"$tmpdir/lid/state"

cat >"$tmpdir/bin/herdr" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
cat "$AGENTS"
SH
cat >"$tmpdir/bin/systemd-inhibit" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exec sleep 300
SH
cat >"$tmpdir/bin/omarchy-cmd-missing" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exit 1
SH
for command in omarchy-power-present omarchy-system-lock; do
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$tmpdir/bin/$command"
done
chmod +x "$tmpdir/bin"/*
export PATH="$tmpdir/bin:$PATH"

inhibitor_pid() {
  head -n 1 "$pidfile" | cut -d' ' -f1
}

# Two agents are working, then one of them finishes while the other keeps
# working: the lid must stay inhibited throughout.
echo '{"result":{"agents":[{"agent":"claude","agent_status":"working"},{"agent":"codex","agent_status":"working"}]}}' >"$AGENTS"
"$guard" reconcile
first_pid=$(inhibitor_pid)
kill -0 "$first_pid" 2>/dev/null || fail "two working agents hold the lid" "pid $first_pid"

echo '{"result":{"agents":[{"agent":"claude","agent_status":"working"},{"agent":"codex","agent_status":"done"}]}}' >"$AGENTS"
"$guard" reconcile
sleep 0.2
kill -0 "$first_pid" 2>/dev/null ||
  fail "the held inhibitor survives a change in which agents are working" \
    "inhibitor $first_pid was killed and replaced by $(inhibitor_pid); between the two the lid was not inhibited"
pass "the held inhibitor survives a change in which agents are working"
```

Actual output at the PR head (exit 1):

```
inhibitor 235 was killed and replaced by 277; between the two the lid was not inhibited
not ok - the held inhibitor survives a change in which agents are working
```

With the replacement removed (a live inhibitor is kept while any reason applies), the same test passes:

```
ok - the held inhibitor survives a change in which agents are working
```

Ordering detail from a separate run, with a stub `systemd-inhibit` that logs when it starts and when it is signalled (lid closed, AC):

```
## Scenario 1: lid closed, AC, agents 'claude codex' working -> only 'claude' working
   +0.000ms held=1  acquire pid=2523 why=agents working on AC: claude codex
  +20.259ms held=0  release pid=2523 signal=TERM
  +22.319ms held=1  acquire pid=2564 why=agents working on AC: claude
scenario1-gap: zero-held after release at 1790826594.794080
## Scenario 2: lid closed, AC, skip armed + agent working -> skip expires
   +0.000ms held=1  acquire pid=2613 why=manual skip of next lid suspend
  +20.645ms held=0  release pid=2613 signal=TERM
  +22.735ms held=1  acquire pid=2658 why=agents working on AC: claude
scenario2-gap: zero-held after release at 1790826595.448210
```

(The roughly 2 ms gap here is a bash stub's fork and exec. A real `systemd-inhibit` holds nothing until its D-Bus `Inhibit` call has passed polkit and been answered.)

Why the gap suspends: this part comes from reading systemd v262, not from running logind. In `logind-button.c`, a lid close installs a post event source (`button_install_check_event_source`) that re-runs the lid action on every event-loop iteration while the lid is closed. `manager_handle_action` in `logind-action.c` only declines while a `handle-lid-switch` inhibitor exists. The old inhibitor goes away when its fifo hangs up (`inhibitor_dispatch_fifo`). The replacement `systemd-inhibit` is only forked after the kill, and it still has to connect to the bus and pass polkit. So with the lid closed, undocked and `HandleLidSwitch=suspend` (Omarchy does not override it), logind can act on the gap.
</details>

### The daemon ignores SIGTERM

`trap stop_inhibitor TERM INT EXIT` releases the inhibitor, then the loop retakes it. **Impact:** stopping the unit, including at logout, waits for SIGKILL after the 90 s user-unit stop timeout (source, not run).

**Suggested change:** `trap 'exit 0' TERM INT` and keep `stop_inhibitor` on EXIT.

# Reproducer: the guard daemon keeps running after SIGTERM

Reviewed head: 20a9407982acf04ae068b3faf545782abf49ba56 (also fails identically with the PR merged into quattro 8b4eae66).

`cmd_daemon` installs `trap stop_inhibitor TERM INT EXIT`. The TERM/INT handler releases the inhibitor but does not exit, so the `while true` loop carries on, calls `reconcile` again and takes a new inhibitor. systemd only escalates to SIGKILL after the stop timeout.

Save as `test/shell.d/lid-guard-stop-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/lid-guard-stop-test.sh`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

guard="$ROOT/bin/omarchy-system-lid-guard"
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
daemon_pid=""

cleanup() {
  [[ -n $daemon_pid ]] && kill -KILL -- "-$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -rf "$tmpdir"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

export HOME="$tmpdir/home" XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$tmpdir/runtime"
export OMARCHY_LID_STATE_GLOB="$tmpdir/lid/state"
mkdir -p "$HOME" "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR" "$tmpdir/bin" "$tmpdir/lid"
echo "state:      open" >"$tmpdir/lid/state"

cat >"$tmpdir/bin/herdr" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo '{"result":{"agents":[{"agent":"claude","agent_status":"working"}]}}'
SH
cat >"$tmpdir/bin/systemd-inhibit" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exec sleep 300
SH
cat >"$tmpdir/bin/omarchy-cmd-missing" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exit 1
SH
for command in omarchy-power-present omarchy-system-lock; do
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$tmpdir/bin/$command"
done
chmod +x "$tmpdir/bin"/*
export PATH="$tmpdir/bin:$PATH"

# Run the daemon in its own process group, the way systemd runs it in its own
# cgroup, and wait until it holds the inhibitor.
setsid "$guard" daemon &
daemon_pid=$!
for _ in {1..50}; do
  [[ -s $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-lid-guard/inhibit.pid ]] && break
  sleep 0.1
done
[[ -s $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-lid-guard/inhibit.pid ]] || fail "daemon takes the inhibitor"

# systemctl stop sends SIGTERM to every process in the unit (KillMode=control-group).
kill -TERM -- "-$daemon_pid"
for _ in {1..30}; do
  kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
  sleep 0.1
done
if kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
  fail "the guard exits on SIGTERM" \
    "daemon $daemon_pid still running 3s after SIGTERM; pidfile now names $(head -n 1 "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-lid-guard/inhibit.pid" 2>/dev/null || echo nothing)"
fi
pass "the guard exits on SIGTERM"
```

Actual output at the PR head (exit 1):

```
Terminated                 sleep "$INTERVAL"
daemon 301 still running 3s after SIGTERM; pidfile now names 352 23900288
not ok - the guard exits on SIGTERM
```

The pidfile names a new inhibitor (352) started after the SIGTERM. A separate run that waited 7 seconds found the daemon still running and one inhibitor acquired 16 ms after the SIGTERM.

With the TERM/INT trap changed to exit (`trap stop_inhibitor EXIT` plus `trap 'exit 0' TERM INT`), the same test passes:

```
ok - the guard exits on SIGTERM
```
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### The guard locks a docked (clamshell) lid close

`reconcile` calls `omarchy-system-lock` on every guarded open-to-closed transition. `omarchy-system-lid-close` deliberately skips that when an external monitor is connected, and `lid-close-test.sh` asserts it. **Impact:** with an agent working on AC or a skip armed, closing the lid to work on an external display locks the session within one poll (5 s). In the undocked case the guard's lock only duplicates the Hyprland lid bind's lock.

**Suggested change:** Drop the guard's lock, or gate it on `! omarchy-hw-external-monitors` like `omarchy-system-lid-close`.

### The new unit is not in the package recipe

The `omarchy-settings` PKGBUILD in omacom/omarchy-pkgs installs each user unit explicitly and has no `omarchy-lid-guard.service`, and `test/shell.d/config-test.sh` `package_defaults` does not list it either. **Impact** (source reading, not run): `enable-user-units.sh` enables its user units in one `systemctl --user enable --now`, and systemd rejects the whole list when one unit is missing, so a new install would get none of them. The migration prints an error and is still marked done.

**Suggested change:** Add the unit to `package_defaults` together with a matching omarchy-pkgs change, and consider enabling the guard in its own command.

</details>

# Reproducer: the guard locks a docked (clamshell) lid close

Reviewed head: 20a9407982acf04ae068b3faf545782abf49ba56 (also fails identically with the PR merged into quattro 8b4eae66).

`omarchy-system-lid-close` locks only when the lid is closed and no external monitor is connected. A docked close is clamshell mode, and `test/shell.d/lid-close-test.sh` asserts that it does not lock. The guard's `reconcile` calls `omarchy-system-lock` whenever a reason applies (agent working on AC, or skip armed) and it saw the lid go from open to closed. It never checks for an external monitor.

Save as `test/shell.d/lid-guard-docked-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/lid-guard-docked-test.sh`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

guard="$ROOT/bin/omarchy-system-lid-guard"
tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)

cleanup() {
  local pidfile="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-lid-guard/inhibit.pid"
  [[ -f $pidfile ]] && kill "$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$pidfile")" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -rf "$tmpdir"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

export HOME="$tmpdir/home" XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$tmpdir/runtime" CALL_LOG="$tmpdir/calls"
export OMARCHY_LID_STATE_GLOB="$tmpdir/lid/state"
mkdir -p "$HOME" "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR" "$tmpdir/bin" "$tmpdir/lid"
: >"$CALL_LOG"

# Docked: lid closed with an external monitor connected, on AC, while herdr
# reports a working agent.
cat >"$tmpdir/bin/herdr" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo '{"result":{"agents":[{"agent":"claude","agent_status":"working"}]}}'
SH
cat >"$tmpdir/bin/systemd-inhibit" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exec sleep 300
SH
cat >"$tmpdir/bin/omarchy-cmd-missing" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exit 1
SH
for command in omarchy-power-present omarchy-hw-external-monitors omarchy-hw-laptop-closed omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell; do
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$tmpdir/bin/$command"
done
cat >"$tmpdir/bin/omarchy-system-lock" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo omarchy-system-lock >>"$CALL_LOG"
SH
chmod +x "$tmpdir/bin"/*
export PATH="$tmpdir/bin:$PATH"

# The existing lid handler leaves a docked close unlocked: that is clamshell
# mode, still in use on the external display.
"$ROOT/bin/omarchy-system-lid-close"
[[ ! -s $CALL_LOG ]] || fail "docked lid close does not lock" "$(cat "$CALL_LOG")"
pass "docked lid close does not lock"

# The guard sees the same close on its next poll.
echo "state:      open" >"$tmpdir/lid/state"
"$guard" reconcile
echo "state:      closed" >"$tmpdir/lid/state"
"$guard" reconcile
[[ ! -s $CALL_LOG ]] || fail "guarded docked lid close does not lock" "calls: $(tr '\n' ' ' <"$CALL_LOG")"
pass "guarded docked lid close does not lock"
```

Actual output at the PR head (exit 1):

```
ok - docked lid close does not lock
calls: omarchy-system-lock 
not ok - guarded docked lid close does not lock
```

With the guard's lock gated on `! omarchy-hw-external-monitors`, the same test passes:

```
ok - docked lid close does not lock
ok - guarded docked lid close does not lock
```

